title: AI-based assessment of cellular phenotypes from high content imaging as a biomarker to guide treatment selection for RA
summary:
Rheumatoid arthritis is a long-term condition causing painful joint inflammation that affects millions of people. To treat it, doctors use special drugs that calm down the immune system. However, these drugs work differently for everyone, and it is often hard to predict which one is best for a specific person.

The goal of this study is to identify specific "fingerprints" in a patient’s immune cells. We want to find out if certain patterns in these cells can predict whether a therapy will be successful even before it begins.

We analyze blood samples from patients at three different stages: before they start a new medication, and then after 12 and 24 weeks of treatment. We are comparing three different types of modern arthritis medications. Using advanced imaging and computer technology, we look at how the cells are shaped, how they communicate, and how they react to the medicine.

By combining these cell analyses with real-world clinical data, such as blood tests and joint scans, we want to create a clearer picture of how treatment works. This information will be used to develop an AI-based tool. This tool is designed to help doctors choose the most effective, personalized therapy for each patient much faster than before.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Adult Patients with rheumatoid arthritis, classified according to the 2010 ACR/EULAR criteria
who failed sufficient response to Methotrexate as a first line drug, classified by ACR20
response criteria.
- Follow-up of clinical treatment response to b/tsDMARD three and six months following
treatment start date is possible.
-The patient has signed the written informed consent form (EK Nr. 1075/2021, register for rheumatic diseases)
Exclusion criteria:
- Patient diagnosis does not meet the classification criteria for RA.
- Reason for discontinuation of Methotrexate therapy is not failure of sufficient treatment
response as classified by ACR20 criteria.
- Clinical information is not available for the time point of sampling.
- Clinical follow-up information is not available for three and six months after starting
b/tsDMARD treatment.
- Sample does not contain viable intact cells.
- Glucocorticoid pulse therapy at the date of sampling.
- Patient has not signed the written informed consent form (EK Nr. 1075/2021).
